decision: Owner decisions of 2026-10-22: Stripe is the payment provider. Business and Enterprise accounts may run and read Repo Audit on imported repositories for diagnosis only. Every repair is done in-house: the customer sees the price in a pop-up and, on agreeing, Stripe holds the amount on their card and charges it when the repair is delivered. The price comes from a published rate table applied to the findings the customer picks. A repair is delivered as a pull request to the customer's repository when KoreLumina has write access, otherwise as a download. KoreLumina imports any kind of repository.
source: The owner's conversation with Claude on 2026-10-22, after comparing the landing page and docs/architecture/ENGINEERING_SPEC_V1.md chapter 14 with the code.

missions.title: Import any repository
missions.objective: KoreLumina imports a repository from any git host or an uploaded archive, in any language, records that it was imported (not built in KoreLumina), and says honestly which analyses apply to it.
risks: Private repositories need an access token; it must live only in Runtime's secret store and never be written to project files, logs or reports.
Advisory checks for non-JavaScript ecosystems need an outside vulnerability database (for example OSV); running against it needs the owner's approval.
Archives from customers are untrusted: path traversal, symlinks and size bombs must be refused.

tasks.title: Import from any git host over HTTPS
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and self-hosted git URLs import
A private repository imports with a token the customer provides, and the token is never stored in the project or shown again

tasks.title: Import from an uploaded archive
acceptanceCriteria: zip and tar.gz import
Entries outside the project folder, symlinks out of it, and archives over the size limit are refused with a reason

tasks.title: Every project records its origin
acceptanceCriteria: A project is marked imported (with its source) or built in KoreLumina
Diagnosis and paid repair are offered only for imported projects

tasks.title: Detect the ecosystem of every package in the repository
acceptanceCriteria: Node, Python, Go, Rust, Java and Kotlin (Maven, Gradle), .NET, PHP, Ruby, Swift, Dart and Flutter, C and C++ (CMake) are recognised from their manifests
Anything else is reported as unrecognised, never guessed

tasks.title: Repository Intelligence analyses each recognised ecosystem
acceptanceCriteria: Dependency manifests and lockfiles are read for each recognised ecosystem
Secret and code risk scans run on every text file whatever the language
A category the engine cannot check for an ecosystem is reported as not checked and never counted as passing

validationPlan: One repository per recognised ecosystem imports and audits with no false build failure

missions.title: Diagnosis for Business and Enterprise; repair stays in-house
missions.objective: Business and Enterprise customers run and read Repo Audit on their imported repositories to diagnose them. Fix plans, repair drafts and applying changes stay with in-house engineers, enforced by Runtime.
risks: This changes the access policy in ENGINEERING_SPEC_V1.md chapter 14 (customers never run the engine). It needs an ADR the owner accepts before the code changes.
Plan roles are trustworthy only once MS-2026-0003 assigns them through Stripe's webhook.

tasks.title: ADR: customer diagnosis, in-house repair
acceptanceCriteria: States who may run, read, plan and apply
The owner accepts it
ENGINEERING_SPEC_V1.md chapter 14 and LANDING_CONTRACT.md agree with it

tasks.title: Runtime authorises audit by role and project
acceptanceCriteria: business and enterprise may start audits and read reports of their own imported projects only
Fix plans, repair drafts and apply routes refuse every customer role
Tests cover each role on each route

tasks.title: Customer diagnosis view
acceptanceCriteria: A Business or Enterprise customer sees score, grade, categories and findings, and can export the client report
No fix plan or repair control is shown to them
Built in the Knowledge Operations design and approved visually

tasks.title: Landing page says the same
acceptanceCriteria: The Repo Audit tooltip and FAQ say diagnosis on Business and Enterprise, repair by KoreLumina engineers

validationPlan: A business caller is refused the fix-plan route and allowed the report route

missions.title: Paid repair: priced, held, repaired in-house, delivered
missions.objective: From a diagnosis, the customer picks findings to repair, sees the price, and agrees. Stripe holds the amount, the job lands in the In-House Dev queue, engineers repair it, and delivery as a pull request or download captures the charge.
risks: Needs MS-2026-0003: a Stripe customer with a saved payment method, and Stripe keys only in Runtime's environment.
A card hold expires after about 7 days; a job expected to take longer is charged on agreement, and the pop-up says so before they agree.
Pushing a pull request needs write access the customer grants; without it the repair is delivered as a download.

tasks.title: The owner publishes the repair rate table
acceptanceCriteria: A price per finding severity and category, and a minimum per job, set by the owner and versioned
Every quote records the rate table version it used

tasks.title: Repair pop-up
acceptanceCriteria: Shows the chosen findings, the price from the rate table, when the card is charged, and what is delivered
Nothing is held or charged until the customer agrees
Built in the Knowledge Operations design and approved visually

tasks.title: Stripe hold and capture
acceptanceCriteria: Agreeing creates a manual-capture PaymentIntent on the saved card
Delivery captures it; cancelling releases it
Every Stripe event is verified by signature and recorded once

tasks.title: Engagement record in Runtime
acceptanceCriteria: Holds customer, project, chosen findings, quote, payment state, assignee, status and full history
Statuses: requested, held, in progress, in review, delivered, cancelled

tasks.title: In-House Dev Engagements queue
acceptanceCriteria: Engineers see, take and work each engagement, with its audit and fix plan one click away
The console from MS-2026-0011 (Tools, Projects, Attention) sits beside the queue
Approved visually and certified

tasks.title: Delivery
acceptanceCriteria: A pull request to the customer's repository when KoreLumina has write access, otherwise a download of the repaired project
A re-audit after repair is attached to the delivery
Delivery captures the held charge

validationPlan: A Stripe test-mode repair goes from agreement to hold to delivery to capture
